newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan MOF says to cut deposit rate to 2.8 pct.
newsitem.headline: Japan MOF says to cut deposit rate to 2.8 pct.

text.p: The Ministry of Finance (MOF) said on Monday it will cut the interest rate it pays to other ministries on their long-term deposits by 0.1 percentage point to 2.8 percent, effective from Friday.
The move follows a fall in the coupon rate of the latest auctioned 10-year Japanese government bonds (JGBs), on which the deposit rate is customarily set.
The coupon rate for the JGB to be issued on July 22 fell to 2.6 percent from 2.7 percent for the June issue.

The MOF's Trust Fund Bureau channels funds raised via deposits made by the Health Ministry and the Posts and Telecommunications Ministry to government-affiliated financial institutions and other quasi-governmental bodies through the fiscal investment and loan programme (FILP).
The programme is widely known as Japan's "second budget" for the role it plays in supplementing the state budget.
